name: Autolus Therapeutics plc

profile.description: Autolus Therapeutics plc is a clinical-stage-turned-commercial biopharmaceutical company developing next-generation, precisely engineered T-cell therapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. Its lead product, AUCATZYL (obecabtagene autoleucel), received FDA approval in November 2024 for adult relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and subsequently gained UK and EU conditional marketing authorizations. Headquartered in London, UK, with manufacturing and clinical operations spanning the US and Europe.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): AUCATZYL's FDA approval (November 2024) and subsequent UK launch (January 2026) mark Autolus's transformation from a purely clinical-stage company into a commercial one, generating $74.3M in full-year 2025 net product revenue and guided to $120-135M in 2026 (62-82% growth), with gross margin turning positive ($1.6M) in Q1 2026 for the first time [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI-powered drug discovery or AI-driven operational savings was found. Market Share (1/2): AUCATZYL is a newer entrant against established CD19-directed CAR-T therapies in relapsed/refractory B-ALL, differentiated by a favorable safety profile, but has not yet demonstrated category-leading revenue or share versus larger incumbents. Product Pipeline (2/2): Four named, phase-specific clinical programs — CATULUS (pediatric r/r ALL, Phase 2), LUMINA (lupus nephritis, Phase 2), BOBCAT (progressive MS, Phase 1), and CARLYSLE (severe refractory SLE, Phase 1) — provide specific pipeline visibility beyond the core oncology franchise [2][3]. R&D Intensity (1/1): As an early-commercial biotech running four concurrent clinical programs against $75.4M of FY2025 revenue, R&D spend is well above typical industry-revenue ratios.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Autolus's purpose — engineering precisely targeted, controlled T-cell therapies to 'transform outcomes' for cancer and autoimmune disease patients — is specific to its proprietary modular T-cell programming platform and connects clearly to patient impact, though the company (founded 2014, first approval 2024) has not yet accumulated the multi-decade track record needed for a higher score [1]. Community Impact (0/2): No specific dollar-quantified charitable or community programs were identified. Employee Retention (0/2): Autolus announced a reduction in force affecting approximately 13% of its workforce in April 2026 as part of a cost-reduction initiative, a direct negative retention signal [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider stock-purchase data was identified in available research.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics (growth-stock weighting; Forward PEG excluded as not meaningful given negative earnings). D/E of 0% (zero total debt against ~$1.6B equity) scores a full 1.0, but ROE of -29.6%, negative Forward P/E of -2.4x, and profit margin of roughly -381% (FY2025 net loss of $287.5M against $75.4M revenue) all score 0 given the company remains pre-profitability [1][4]. Revenue growth metrics are extraordinary in percentage terms (FY2025 revenue of $75.4M vs. $10.1M in FY2024) but reflect the AUCATZYL commercial launch ramp from a near-zero base rather than steady-state operating momentum, and should be read with that caveat despite capping the formula score at 1.0. Liquidity is adequate but thin: $1.44 price x 1.38M average daily volume ≈ $2.0M/day, above the $1M floor but not deeply liquid.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Autolus's business — engineering and GMP-manufacturing living cell therapies, running FDA/EMA-regulated clinical trials, and commercial-scale cell processing — is deeply physical and biologically grounded, structurally immune to AI substitution; no analyst commentary was found suggesting AI threatens cell-therapy commercialization or manufacturing. AI Opportunity (0/1): No evidence of AI-driven drug discovery, AI-generated revenue, or AI-quantified savings was found for Autolus specifically.

infinite_game.summary: Autolus displays a partially-formed infinite-game profile. Its mission to transform outcomes for cancer and autoimmune patients through a proprietary T-cell platform is genuine and referenced in pipeline strategy, and the company has continued to invest in four parallel clinical programs even while managing capital constraints. But a recent 13% workforce reduction signals financial pressure rather than clear strategic courage, no culture or trust evidence was found, and the company — only two years into commercialization — has not yet faced the test of a full economic or competitive cycle.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Autolus's purpose of engineering precisely controlled T-cell therapies to transform outcomes in cancer and autoimmune disease is genuine and connects directly to patient benefit, referenced consistently across its four-program pipeline, but the company's short public history (first approval in 2024) means it has not yet been tested through a market cycle or crisis [1][2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The April 2026 reduction in force affecting approximately 13% of the workforce is a direct instability signal, and no offsetting evidence of high employee trust, tenure, or psychological safety was found [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence was found of Autolus publicly framing competing CAR-T developers' strengths as a source of self-improvement in available research.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Autolus transitioned from a purely clinical-stage biotech to a commercial-stage company following AUCATZYL's approval, building out manufacturing and commercial infrastructure — a meaningful operational evolution, though an expected progression for any biotech reaching approval rather than an existential pivot away from its core science [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Autolus has continued to fund four concurrent clinical programs spanning oncology and autoimmune indications even while implementing a 13% workforce reduction to preserve capital — evidence of prioritizing pipeline breadth, though the layoffs also reflect financial necessity rather than unambiguous strategic choice [2][3].

investment_thesis: Autolus has crossed the inflection from clinical-stage to commercial-stage biotech: AUCATZYL generated $74.3M in FY2025 net product revenue and $26.2M in Q1 2026 (versus $9.0M a year earlier), with 2026 guidance of $120-135M implying 62-82% growth, and gross margin turned positive for the first time in Q1 2026 as manufacturing efficiency and treatment-center volume both scale [1]. The company has activated 67 treatment centers with a target of 80+ by year-end 2026, and a four-program pipeline (CATULUS, LUMINA, BOBCAT, CARLYSLE) spanning oncology and autoimmune indications provides multi-year clinical and commercial catalysts beyond the core B-ALL indication [2]. The physical, biologically-grounded cell-therapy manufacturing and regulatory process is structurally immune to AI disruption.
thesis_continued: The financial profile remains that of an early-commercial biotech: FY2025 net loss of $287.5M against $75.4M of revenue, negative ROE of -29.6%, and a negative forward P/E reflecting continued unprofitability. An April 2026 reduction in force affecting 13% of the workforce underscores ongoing capital discipline pressure even as the commercial ramp proceeds, and thin trading liquidity (~$2.0M/day dollar volume) adds volatility risk. With Inspiration (2/10) and Infinite Game (4/10) scores reflecting a short public track record and limited culture evidence, Autolus screens as a WATCH — a name whose commercial execution and pipeline readouts over the next several quarters will determine whether the recent gross-margin inflection is durable.
key_catalysts: Continued AUCATZYL commercial ramp toward the $120-135M 2026 guidance range as treatment centers expand from 67 toward the 80+ year-end target
Sustained positive gross margin (achieved for the first time in Q1 2026) as manufacturing volume and efficiency scale further
Pipeline readouts from the CATULUS, LUMINA, BOBCAT, and CARLYSLE trials, any of which could expand Autolus's addressable indications beyond adult r/r B-ALL
key_risks: Continued cash burn (FY2025 net loss of $287.5M) against a still-small revenue base creates ongoing capital-raise or dilution risk despite the recent 13% workforce reduction
Thin trading liquidity (~$2.0M/day dollar volume) leaves the stock vulnerable to sharp price moves on clinical or commercial news
Competitive pressure from established CD19-directed CAR-T therapies with larger commercial infrastructure could limit AUCATZYL's share gains in relapsed/refractory B-ALL
